articles.author: rowan-vale
articles.title: Five touchdowns for Ninjaskamara, one more game for Mossdeep
articles.dek: The Eclipse beat Dewford 40–3 behind 279 yards from their leading back, then learned Marshall Flock faces a two-week absence.

body.text: Ninjaskamara gave Mossdeep five touchdowns and Dewford several different problems. He ran twenty times for 189 yards, caught two passes for ninety more and scored on five of those twenty-two touches. The Eclipse won their playoff opener 40–3, advancing to a conference championship meeting with Sunyshore after a performance that made their earlier three-point win over the Breakers feel very distant.

Mossdeep gained 489 yards, including 247 on the ground. Dewford gained 122. The first three Eclipse possessions all ended in touchdowns, and the defense kept the Breakers out of the end zone throughout. A team that finished the regular season 17–0 returned from its bye with its principal offensive players producing immediately. There was little opportunity for the familiar discussion about whether an extra week off had disturbed anyone's timing.

The result still came with a significant availability change. Marshall Flock is listed for two weeks in the latest injury record, joining Poury Holt, whose counter is now four. The game report does not establish which play caused Flock's injury. Mossdeep heads toward Sunyshore with a dominant new result and a confirmed defensive absence to account for; both belong in the assessment of what this win means.
Three possessions, three touchdowns

Dram Marino completed sixteen of twenty-two passes for 242 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. He found Ninjaskamara for a twenty-four-yard touchdown with 3:40 left in the opening quarter, finishing a seventy-four-yard drive. The back's first scoring contribution came as a receiver, a useful warning for a Dewford defense that would soon spend much of the afternoon dealing with his rushing workload.

Ninjaskamara then scored on a thirty-eight-yard run with 1:23 remaining in the first quarter. That possession covered sixty-six yards. The two opening drives produced fourteen points through different finishes: one passing play to the back and one long carry. Dewford had already been required to defend the full distance twice, without a turnover or a short field doing the preparation work for Mossdeep.

The third scoring drive went eighty-three yards and ended with Marino's ten-yard touchdown pass to Accel BeckhmJr at 3:12 of the second quarter. Vinathorn missed the extra point, leaving the score 20–0. Accel finished with six catches on seven targets for ninety-one yards, the largest receiving total on the team by a single yard. Ninjaskamara's spectacular scoring line had substantial help.

Marino also completed all three of his attempts toward Ninjulio Jones, who gained twenty-five yards. Gronkaludon added twenty-one receiving yards on two catches. Those shorter connections mattered because the offense kept moving between its explosive plays. The opening three drives covered 223 yards in total, a measure of sustained offense as well as individual speed. Dewford could not rely on one successful tackle near midfield to end the immediate danger.
The interruption before halftime

body.caption: Dram Marino and Accel BeckhmJr combined for six completions, ninety-one yards and a touchdown. Imagined sideline conversation.

body.text: The Breakers did produce a defensive stop before the break. Ambipom sacked Marino during a six-play possession that gained twenty-six yards, and Mossdeep punted. It was the Eclipse's only punt of the game. For Dewford, that sequence offered a brief example of the pressure and down-to-down resistance required to slow the home offense. It arrived after the three touchdown drives had established a twenty-point deficit.

Dewford's own passing game never developed a comparable answer. Frosmoth completed six of fourteen attempts for ninety-two yards, threw an interception and took five sacks for thirty-six lost yards. Those negative plays repeatedly increased the distance the Breakers needed to cover. Against a defense already limiting the rushing attack, that was an expensive way to spend an offensive possession.

Excadrill carried ten times for twenty-seven yards. Watchog added nine on three carries, and the team's final rushing total was thirty yards. Dewford had advanced from the wild-card round by holding Eterna without a touchdown and finishing two short opportunities through Watchog. This game required longer scoring drives, with Mossdeep taking an early lead and giving the Breakers very little ground production to support them.

The difference from the clubs' 24–21 regular-season meeting was therefore visible well beyond the margin. Mossdeep entered halftime ahead 20–0, its defense had kept Dewford from answering any of the early scores, and its offense had repeatedly traveled most of the field. The earlier close game remained a valid reason to take the Breakers seriously before kickoff. The new possessions supplied a much stronger description of this particular afternoon.
A third-down catch becomes sixty-six yards

Ninjaskamara's second receiving touchdown came on third-and-eight with 4:44 left in the third quarter. Marino found him for a sixty-six-yard score. A down on which Dewford could have ended a possession instead became the longest touchdown of the game. The back finished with only two catches, but both reached the end zone and together accounted for ninety yards.

That efficiency makes the receiving line easy to misunderstand if it is read only as a small number of targets or catches. Ninjaskamara's passing-game involvement produced two entire scoring plays, including the third-down answer that widened the lead after halftime. Dewford needed a stop to begin reducing the deficit. Mossdeep extended it before the Breakers could make their next possession a meaningful response to a close score.

Luvrelle Revis intercepted Frosmoth at 3:30 of the third quarter and returned the ball eighteen yards. Ninjaskamara scored on a one-yard run at 2:03, pushing the lead to 34–0. The interception gave Mossdeep another opportunity, and the offense finished it. By then the back had scored twice through the air and twice on the ground, with his final rushing touchdown still ahead.

Derrat Brooks led the defensive pressure with three sacks. Joey Sporeter and Bearon Donald added one apiece. Their contributions gave the pass defense more than a single interception to show for its work. Frosmoth was repeatedly forced to absorb a loss before the Breakers could establish the passing volume required by the score. Dewford's six completions were too few to sustain that pursuit.

body.text: Dewford's field goal and Mossdeep's final answer

Camerupt made a thirty-one-yard field goal with twenty-seven seconds remaining in the third quarter, getting Dewford onto the scoreboard at 34–3. The Breakers had avoided a shutout, but the field goal left them needing several additional possessions and almost immediate defensive stops. Mossdeep's next scoring drive removed even that narrow possibility of a late change in the game's character.

Ninjaskamara scored on an eight-yard run with 4:31 left in the fourth quarter. The extra point missed, producing the eventual 40–3 score. Vinathorn finished four-for-six on extra points. Those two misses did not threaten this result, but they are concrete items for a team preparing to play a stronger opponent with a championship berth available. A comfortable margin does not make a failed conversion disappear from the report.
We punted, we missed two kicks, and they got three points. There is enough there for the meeting.
body.speaker: Michael Dorrill

body.text: The coach had just won by thirty-seven, but his three complaints were all specific. Mossdeep can address those details before a game in which one missed conversion or one failed possession could decide the result.

Shawn Mareman helped finish the afternoon with eight carries for fifty-eight yards. On the closing possession he converted third-and-one with a fourteen-yard run and added an eleven-yard gain. Mossdeep covered fifty-four yards while consuming the final 3:38. Ninjaskamara contributed another nine-yard carry during that sequence, bringing his rushing total to 189 without needing another score to underline it.
Sunyshore gets the next opportunity

Mossdeep now hosts the Starseekers, who beat Petalburg 24–10 and have won twice in the playoffs. The Eclipse won the regular-season meeting 27–3. That result and the new Dewford performance make Mossdeep the clear favorite, while Flock's two-week injury entry gives the coming preparation a specific personnel concern. The confirmed absence deserves attention without inventing a replacement lineup or a medical timetable beyond the reported counter.

Dewford leaves with a playoff win over Eterna and a divisional loss in which it could not generate enough offense to challenge the top seed. A full offseason assessment can wait for the season review. The explanation of this game is already substantial: five sacks allowed, thirty rushing yards, no touchdowns and a defense that surrendered three long scoring drives before halftime.

For Mossdeep, Ninjaskamara's 279 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns supplied the headline. Marino's clean passing, Accel's ninety-one receiving yards, Brooks's three sacks and the closing work from Mareman explain the support around it. The Eclipse are one win from the championship game after producing the most complete performance of the divisional round.
